Question: Based on the NIST SP 800-207 Zero Trust Architecture diagram in Solicitation 03 (02_Zero_Trust_Architecture_Specs.pdf), how do the Policy Engine (PE), Policy Administrator (PA), and Policy Enforcement Point (PEP) interact before granting enclave access?

payload.answer:
Based on `02_Zero_Trust_Architecture_Specs.pdf`, the Policy Engine (PE), Policy Administrator (PA), and Policy Enforcement Point (PEP) interact through the following flow before granting access to the Protected Enterprise Enclave:

1. **Policy Engine (PE) to Policy Administrator (PA) [Control Plane]:** 
   The PE evaluates continuous device posture, BeyondCorp context-aware access levels, and Chronicle threat intelligence feeds. Based on this evaluation, the PE signals the PA to mint short-lived mTLS / OIDC session tokens.

2. **Policy Administrator (PA) to Policy Enforcement Point (PEP) [Data Plane]:** 
   The PEP (consisting of the Identity-Aware Proxy [IAP] and Envoy Service Mesh ingress gateways / BeyondCorp IAP + mTLS Mesh) terminates all incoming traffic from the untrusted subject and device. The PEP then grants per-request access to the protected enclave resources **only upon verification from the PA**. 

*(Note: As part of continuous telemetry, every allow/deny decision made by the PEP also streams to the Google SecOps SIEM).*
